thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated-pool node gpu-23 in pool sablecore-east1 reporting repeated PCIe AER/ECC spikes — 5+ device errors in 10m. potential tenant impact (SableCore / sable-enterprise). Severity: potential customer-facing degradation. Paging on-call now. :rotating_light:

Maria R.: seeing the bot, grabbing on-call. I'm on mobile, can someone pull p95 latency and error-rate for sable-enterprise?

Julian (SRE): looking. quick peek from observability: sable-enterprise request_errors +12% in last 7m, p95 gen latency from 1.2s -> 2.6s. model-worker restart counts +3 on nodes colocated with gpu-23.

Kevin T.: I'm taking primary oncall. Maria please handoff.

Maria R.: handing off to Kevin — details: node gpu-23 is in dedicated pool "sablecore-east1-ded1". Host-level logs show repeated `pcie_aer` entries and `gpu_reset` events. Customers seeing 5xx on long-running streaming sessions. Liz, do we have a CS contact for SableCore on call?

Liz (Customer Success): yes, SableCore on-call is @sable-ops (Anish). I've pinged them via phone and DM with brief. They confirm impact: intermittent 5xx for batch/streaming jobs started in last 15m. They're asking for ETA and mitigation.

Ari (Runtime): from runtime perspective, live-evicting tenants from gpu-23 and moving workloads to warm spares is safest. I can trigger fallback routing to pool-surge-east1 and instruct the runtime to use quantized fallback model `gpt-light-q4` for current sessions to reduce memory pressure. That should lower restart rate.

Harpreet (HW Ops): I'll open a hardware ticket and start remote diagnostics. If it's PCIe fabric it's likely a host-level component fail. We may need to RMA the host. ETA for physical on-site replace depends on vendor, but prelim check first.

Sam (Cloud): note — this host is currently a preemptible/spot-backed instance. We saw a spot reclaim 10m earlier in same AZ but it returned; suspicious. I'll check provider eviction events for that host.

Julian (SRE): plan proposal: 1) mark gpu-23 as draining for new allocations 2) live-migrate existing sable-enterprise GPUs off gpu-23 (serially) 3) route new allocation policy to pool-surge-east1 until healthy 4) notify customer and keep CS updated. Anyone object?

Kevin T.: +1. execute. Maria please coordinate with CS. Ari run live-evict command when ready. Harpreet, please escalate to vendor after your diag. OpsBot, annotate incident timeline.

Ari (Runtime): running commands now. command log: ```
# mark node drain
rpoolctl node set-state gpu-23 drain --reason "pci_aer_spike"
# evict tenants (dry-run shown, then exec)
rpoolctl tenant migrate --node gpu-23 --target pool-surge-east1 --filter tenant=sable-enterprise --concurrency 2
```

incident-bot: ACTION: Node gpu-23 state -> DRAINING (by Ari). Eviction job queued (job id 682134).

Julian (SRE): monitoring eviction progress. first tenant migrated successfully (sess-9932), KV cache warmed on new node. second migration showing brief increase in 503s for that session (duration ~18s) then recovered. overall error rate starting to trend down.

Liz (Customer Success): Anish (SableCore) confirms they see degraded job starts still for older sessions, but new jobs are routing fine to fallback. They're asking about a timeline for replacement and whether logs will be preserved for forensic.

Harpreet (HW Ops): remote diag results: `lspci` shows AER errors tied to device 0000:3b:00.0. Kernel logs: `GPU 0: AER severity corrected` and occasional `GPU reset due to AER`. I'm opening ticket with vendor (ticket: VEND-88192). Collecting dmesg and nvml tech logs now.

Sam (Cloud): vendor confirms this hardware has had a similar failure pattern in the cluster over last 30d (rare but recurring). They recommend host replacement rather than repeated reboots — we'll request a replacement instance. I can optionally spin up an on-demand host in same pool to keep capacity while we RMA.

Kevin T.: do that. Ari leave the drain state until Harpreet or I say otherwise. Keep migrations conservative to avoid causing cascade. We should also temporarily bump routing weight to dedicated fallback pools for sable-enterprise to 80% until full replace. Maria coordinate with billing/ops if extra capacity incurs cost.

Maria R.: confirmed. Notifying billing and tagging this incident for cost review. Liz, please send templated update to Anish: short summary, mitigation (migrated to fallback & quantized model), expected HW replace window (TBD but starting vendor RMA now), and preservation of logs.

Liz (Customer Success): sent update to SableCore: "We've migrated active workloads away from the affected host, routing jobs to fallback pool-surge-east1 and switching to a low-memory model to maintain availability. HW replace ticket opened; we'll preserve logs and follow up with RCA." Anish acknowledged and asked to be notified when a permanent host is replaced.

Julian (SRE): metrics check 10m post-migration: error_rate back down near baseline, p95 latency receding to ~1.4s. There's still a few restart spikes for non-migrated long-running sessions; I'm setting a watch for 30m.

Harpreet (HW Ops): uploaded nvml logs and pxie dumps to ticket. vendor assigned an engineer, earliest swap 10h window due to depot availability. If we want faster, we can request expedited RMA (cost center needed).

Ari (Runtime): follow-up action: we also pushed a runtime fallback flag for sable-enterprise: `USE_QUANT_FALLBACK=true` for 60m window. Command: `rpoolctl config set tenant sable-enterprise fallback_model gpt-light-q4 --ttl 3600`. This was confirmed successful.

OpsBot: NOTE: incident annotated with tag "dedicated-pool-hw". Creating follow-up task: create postmortem and assess fallback policy efficacy.

Kevin T.: handoff to daytime SRE lead. I'm logging off; Julian will own monitoring until hardware replaced. Maria will coordinate cross-org comms. Final immediate checklist: - node drained (done) - tenants migrated (in progress, majority done) - vendor RMA opened (VEND-88192) - CS notified (SableCore) - cost/billing notified (Maria).

Julian (SRE): I'll continue watching for 30-60m. If we see new AER events after eviction, we'll forcibly quiesce the host and remove it from rotation.

Maria R.: thanks team. I'll file the incident ticket and send initial incident note to #postmortems once we stabilize. Scheduling follow-up call with Harpreet, Ari, Liz, and vendor tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

incident-bot: SEVERITY UPDATE: Incident severity set to P2 — customer-visible degradation mitigated, hardware replacement required. Follow-up tasks created: postmortem, billing review, and customer RCA (ticket id: INC-2026-9941). :white_check_mark:
